props.gloss_en: the mishna: everyone slaughters
the mishna: and their slaughter is valid
the mishna: and all of them who slaughtered while others watch them -- their slaughter is valid
'everyone slaughters' is said of ab initio
'and their slaughter is valid' is said of after the fact
the general claim Rav Acha challenges: every 'הכל' in a mishna indicates ab initio
the Temura mishna: everyone substitutes, men and women alike -- though the verse says 'he shall not substitute it' (Lev 27:10)
the Arakhin mishna: everyone vows valuations and is valuated, vows and is vowed -- though 'if you refrain from vowing there is no sin in you' (Deut 23:23) and 'better not to vow' (Eccl 5:4)
R' Meir: better than both [who vows and pays, who vows and does not] is one who does not vow at all
R' Yehuda: better than both is one who vows and pays
Rav Acha: even R' Yehuda said it only of one who says 'this [animal] is [an offering]', but of 'it is upon me' -- no
the converse Rav Ashi challenges: every 'הכל' indicates not-ab-initio
everyone is obligated in sukka; everyone is obligated in tzitzit
everyone lays hands [on the offering], men and women alike -- and the verse says 'he shall lay his hand... and it shall be accepted' (Lev 1:4)
Rav Acha: yes -- there is a 'הכל' of ab initio and a 'הכל' of after the fact
Rabba bar Ulla: the mishna teaches -- everyone slaughters, even an impure person, non-sacred animals [ab initio]
non-sacred food prepared in the purity of sacred food is like sacred food
how does he proceed? he brings a long knife and slaughters with it, so as not to touch the flesh
and sacrificial animals he may not slaughter, lest he touch the flesh; if he did and says 'I am certain I did not touch', his slaughter is valid
except a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor, who even with plain non-sacred animals are invalid even after the fact -- lest they pause, press, or conceal the knife
Zevachim: all the unfit who slaughtered -- their slaughter is valid, by non-priests, women, slaves, the impure, even most-sacred offerings, provided the impure do not touch the flesh
here [Chullin] is the primary source; there [Zevachim] the impure-with-kodshim case was taught only alongside the other unfit
there [Zevachim, which deals with offerings] is the primary source; here it was taught only alongside the impure with non-sacred animals
the impure person was defiled by a corpse -- [and slaughtered] with a reed stalk he examined
rather, he was defiled by a creeping thing
the baraita: one may slaughter with anything -- flint, glass, or a reed stalk
the mishna teaches: everyone slaughters, even a Kuti
Abaye: when is this said? when a Jew stands over him
Abaye: but if [the Jew] goes in and out -- [the Kuti] may not slaughter
and if he slaughtered [unsupervised], one cuts an olive-bulk of meat and gives it to him; if he ate it, his slaughter may be eaten; if not, it is forbidden
the mishna: one who leaves a gentile in his shop while a Jew goes in and out -- [the wine] is permitted
the mishna: the watchman need not sit and guard; even if he goes in and out, [the wine] is permitted
Rava: when is this said? when a Jew goes in and out; but if he came and found him having slaughtered -- he cuts an olive-bulk...
there [the wine] the gentile does not touch; here [the slaughter] he touches
Rav Ashi: the mishna teaches -- everyone slaughters, even a Jewish apostate
an apostate in what respect? in eating carcasses for his appetite
Rava: an apostate who eats carcasses for appetite -- one examines a knife and gives it to him, and his slaughter may be eaten
Rava: if one did not examine and give it -- he may not slaughter; if he did, one examines his knife after; if sound, permitted, if not, forbidden
Ravina: all EXPERTS slaughter -- experts, even if not established [as steady]
Ravina: when known to be able to state the laws of slaughter; if not known -- he may not slaughter, and if he did, one examines him
Ravina (ika damri): all ESTABLISHED [as steady] slaughter -- even if not experts
Ravina (ika damri): when he slaughtered before us two or three times without fainting; otherwise not, lest he faint; if he did and says 'I am certain I did not faint' -- valid

on Rabba bar Ulla's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the impure person with non-sacred animals
on Rabba bar Ulla's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the impure person with sacrificial animals, where he is not before us to ask

on Abaye's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the Kuti

on Rava's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the Kuti
on Rav Ashi's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor
on Rav Ashi's reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the Jewish apostate
on Ravina's first ('experts') reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor
on Ravina's first ('experts') reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the non-experts, where he is not before us to examine
on Ravina's איכא דאמרי ('established') reconstruction, 'and all of them who slaughtered' refers to the deaf-mute, imbecile and minor

objections.gloss_en: ״הכל שוחטין״ -- לכתחלה, ״ושחיטתן כשרה״ -- דיעבד! the first clause permits ab initio, the second validates only after the fact

answered_by.gloss_en: הכי קתני: הכל שוחטין ואפילו טמא בחולין... ובמוקדשים לא ישחוט, ואם שחט -- כשרה (= p_rbu_reading)
הכי קתני: הכל שוחטין ואפילו כותי, כשישראל עומד על גביו; ואם שחט -- חותך כזית (= p_afilu_kuti, p_abaye_omed_al_gabav)
אלא אמר רבא, הכי קתני: ואפילו כותי, כשישראל יוצא ונכנס (= p_rava_yotzei_venichnas; said לדבריו דאביי, 3b.19)
הכי קתני: הכל שוחטין ואפילו ישראל משומד (= p_rav_ashi_reading)
הכי קתני: הכל מומחין שוחטין, ואף על פי שאין מוחזקין (= p_ravina_mumchin)
איכא דאמרי, רבינא: הכל מוחזקין שוחטין, ואף על פי שאין מומחין (= p_ravina_muchzakin, via ika_damri_3b)

objections.gloss_en: וכל ״הכל״ לכתחלה הוא? אלא מעתה הכל ממירין -- הכי נמי דלכתחלה? והא כתיב לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו!

answered_by.gloss_en: התם כדקתני טעמא: לא שהאדם רשאי להמיר, אלא שאם המיר -- מומר וסופג את הארבעים -- the Temura mishna itself qualifies its הכל

objections.gloss_en: אלא הכל מעריכין... נודרין ונידרין, הכי נמי דלכתחלה? והא כתיב וכי תחדל לנדור... וכתיב טוב אשר לא תדור, ותניא (R' Meir / R' Yehuda), ואפילו רבי יהודה לא קאמר אלא בהרי זו (2a.5-2b.1)
וכל ״הכל״ לאו לכתחלה הוא? אלא הכל חייבים בסוכה, הכל חייבין בציצית -- הכי נמי דלאו לכתחלה?

answered_by.gloss_en: ״חייבין״ לא קאמינא -- an obligation is self-evidently ab initio; I do not speak of it

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה הכל סומכין, אחד האנשים ואחד הנשים -- הכי נמי דלאו לכתחלה? והא כתיב וסמך ידו... ונרצה! -- conceded at 2b.4: אין, איכא הכל לכתחלה
אלא ״הכל״ דהכא ממאי דלכתחלה הוא דתקשי לך? דלמא דיעבד הוא, ולא תקשי לך

answered_by.gloss_en: אנא ״שחיטתן כשרה״ קשיא לי: מדקתני שחיטתן כשרה דיעבד, מכלל ד״הכל״ לכתחלה הוא -- דאי דיעבד, תרתי דיעבד למה לי?

objections.gloss_en: ויוצא ונכנס לכתחלה לא? והתנן: המניח נכרי בחנותו וישראל יוצא ונכנס -- מותר! -- rejected: התם מי קתני ״מניח״? ״המניח״ קתני, דיעבד
אלא מהכא: אין השומר צריך להיות יושב ומשמר, אלא אף על פי שיוצא ונכנס -- מותר (the source of Rava's והתנן, replaced)

answered_by.gloss_en: אביי לא אמר כרבא: התם לא נגע, הכא נגע -- the gentile does not touch the wine; the Kuti touches the slaughter (= p_hatam_lo_naga)
